facts.fact_text: The applicants are members of EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union).
EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union) is a trade union.

EĞİTİM-SEN (Eğitim ve Bilim Emekçileri Sendikası – The Education Workers' Trade Union) is a member of KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions).

While the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions was being discussed in the Turkish Parliament, KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) decided to organise meetings in Ankara to protest the bill.

The aim of the meetings organised by KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) was to draw public attention to the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions.

The aim of the meetings organised by KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – The Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) was to achieve the withdrawal of the draft bill to amend the Act on Trade Unions.

On 18 December 2000, the Governorship of Ankara issued a circular providing guidelines on meetings and demonstrations organised in the city of Ankara.
The circular issued by the Governorship of Ankara on 18 December 2000 was issued in accordance with the Law on Meetings and Demonstration Marches (Law no. 2911).

At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration is planned must be informed during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting.

Section 24 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provided that demonstrations and processions which did not comply with the provisions of the Act would be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators had been warned.

According to the circular issued by the Governorship of Ankara on 18 December 2000, which provides guidelines on meetings and demonstrations, Kızılay avenue is not among the permitted areas for demonstrations.
On both occasions (7 June 2001 and 25 June 2001), the demonstrators blocked the main street of the Kızılay district (Atatürk Avenue).
On both occasions (7 June 2001 and 25 June 2001), the demonstrators attempted to march towards the Prime Minister's Office.
On both occasions (7 June 2001 and 25 June 2001), some of the demonstrators attacked the security forces using pavement stones and sticks.
The attacks by demonstrators on security forces caused the injury of seven police officers.
The attacks by demonstrators on security forces caused the destruction of a police vehicle.
